sources.name: NASA Office of Inspector General, IG-22-003 (Artemis program costs)
sources.note: Order of magnitude for an SLS launch; the game uses $2,200M.

sources.name: SpaceX Starship
sources.note: In development; 100 t and $250M are planning values.

sources.name: Game values
sources.note: Launch costs are rounded public prices. Reliability is a game estimate from flight history (Starship is lower because it is still in development). Rule: usable payload = payload to low Earth orbit; the spacecraft's own engine does the rest.

vehicles.name: Falcon 9
vehicles.description: This rocket can fly again and again. It is the cheapest, but it can lift only small robot missions.

vehicles.name: Falcon Heavy
vehicles.description: Like 3 Falcon 9 rockets joined together. It lifts a lot for its price.

vehicles.name: SLS Block 1
vehicles.description: A very big Moon rocket. It flew NASA's Artemis I mission. It is huge and very expensive.

vehicles.name: Starship
vehicles.description: A giant rocket that can fly again and again. It is still being tested. Cheap for its size, but more risky.
